title: Dali contact and the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse

event.summary: The containership Dali struck the Francis Scott Key Bridge; a substantial portion collapsed.

claims.text: The Dali lost electrical power, propulsion and steering while outbound and struck the bridge support pier.
A substantial portion of the bridge collapsed following the contact.

hypotheses.statement: Shipboard power and control losses preceded the bridge contact in the NTSB sequence.
falsifiers: A revised official event sequence placing the power and control losses after the contact.

hypotheses.statement: Bridge debris could constrain local maritime passage until the channel was cleared.
falsifiers: Contemporaneous port passage records showing the relevant channel remained fully open.

hypotheses.statement: Some terminals might have remained reachable through alternate channels despite the bridge debris.
falsifiers: Port authority notices showing that no alternate channel served those terminals at the event time.

unresolvedQuestions: At the event time, which vessel classes and terminals could still be served through alternate channels?
How long did each route restriction last?

exposures.channel: Physical channel access and vessel scheduling
exposures.conditionalImpact: If bridge debris blocked the relevant channel, vessels serving affected terminals would face delays or rerouting; the bridge-collapse claim alone does not measure the duration or economic size.

assessment.whatHappened: The NTSB investigation describes shipboard power and control losses, contact with a support pier, and the subsequent bridge collapse on March 26, 2024.
assessment.whyItMatters: A physical transport disruption can propagate from a single infrastructure failure to port access and shipment timing. This case demonstrates an exposure chain, not a measured trade or current alert.
whatToWatch: Official navigation-channel status at the time
Vessel and terminal activity around the interruption
